changes: Routine lattice validate now reuses a complete fresh PASS when validation identity, material, story files, coverage, and trusted lineage remain unchanged; reuse is locked, fail-closed, auditable, and performs zero command executions without rewriting evidence.
usage: Run node bin/lattice.js validate --story=B-914f --json again after an unchanged PASS; inspect provider, reuse lineage, disposition, and commandExecutions in the JSON result.
expectedOutcome: A repeated routine validation on unchanged story material returns PASS in seconds, reports trusted exact-head or metadata-descendant reuse, and executes zero validation commands.
actualTranscript: Real worktree run exited 0 in 8.6 seconds with provider lattice-verifier-reused, summary Validation PASS reused (trusted-story-metadata-descendant), disposition reused, and commandExecutions=0; done_prepare also reused both routine and DONE-required evidence.
outcomeDiff: No functional difference from the expected outcome; the repeated run produced the intended zero-command trusted reuse.
limitations: Reuse intentionally falls back to real execution for legacy or malformed evidence, changed identity/material/story files, incomplete coverage, dirty untrusted files, non-PASS command execution, or untrusted lineage.
pitfalls: The first post-merge validation legitimately ran the full 45-command plan and its evidence write invalidated same-round reviewer closeout bindings; recovery required a new REVIEW round with one current receipt. Always preserve exec session IDs and use the worktree-local node bin/lattice.js runtime.
